DefaultSheet.Name: New actors use the Edgeheart sheets
DefaultSheet.Hint: A new Character starts with the Edgeheart Sheet (Humanity, Cyber Load, Cyberpsychosis); a new Party starts with the Crew Sheet (Reputation, Edge, and Edge Moves). Existing actors can switch sheets from the sheet configuration icon.

Levelup.Name: Edgeheart Level Up
Levelup.Hint: Removes the HP, Stress, Evasion, Trait, and Multiclass options from Level Up (in Edgeheart they come from Cyberware) and lets Experience and extra Card be picked more times. Applies to the whole world; turning it off restores the original Daggerheart Level Up.

SheetFx.Name: Edgeheart Sheet Look

Humanity.ChatLost:
Death Move: Cyberpsycho

{name} has been lost to Cyberpsychosis{reason}. Choose one:

  • You vanish into the city as a violent urban legend.
  • Your crew is forced to put you down.
  • You burn out in one final act of destruction, saving someone or completing the job at a terrible cost.

Then, create a new character.
Humanity.NoteIntegratedChrome: Integrated Chrome: Cyber Load treated as 1 lower.
Humanity.NoteAnchor: Humanity Anchor: rolled twice and kept the higher.
Humanity.BufferPrompt: Humanity Roll: {total} vs Load {load}. Mark 1 Stress to add +1 and stay in control?
Humanity.EffectDescription:
You don't roll the Hope Die: use only the Fear Die as a d20 + trait; the roll is always with Fear. Features that would require marking Stress can be used without marking Stress.

An ally within Close range can spend a Hope to stabilize you (roll Humanity again). If the scene ends while you're in Cyberpsychosis, reduce your Humanity Die.
Humanity.EffectDuration: Until stabilized or the end of the scene
Humanity.ChatPsycho:
CYBERPSYCHOSIS

{name} lost control. Rolls use only the Fear Die (d20) and are always with Fear; features that would mark Stress don't.
Humanity.SelectHelper: Select the token (or set the character) of the ally who will stabilize.
Humanity.OnlyGMEnd: Only the GM can end Cyberpsychosis without stabilization.
Humanity.OnlyGMRestore: Only the GM can bring back a character lost to Cyberpsychosis.

Help.Humanity: Humanity: starts at d6. It advances once per level (a meaningful bond, an important goal, reclaiming part of yourself, a moment of hope).
Help.Load: Cyber Load: sum of the Cost of all installed cyberware.
Help.Roll: Humanity Roll: if the result is higher than your Load, you stay in control; if it's equal or lower, you enter Cyberpsychosis. It's automatic when you roll with Fear with all Stress marked or with no Hope.
Help.Psycho: Cyberpsychosis: roll only the Fear Die as a d20, always with Fear; features that ask for Stress don't mark it. An ally can spend 1 Hope to stabilize you. Ending the scene like this reduces your Humanity; below d4 you're lost.
Help.Eidolons: Eidolons: drag an Eidolon from the Cyberware compendium onto the sheet and use Mobilize. While synced, HP, Evasion, Thresholds, Armor, and weapons are the frame's (weapons use your Interface), the Sync Cost adds to your Load, and the Competency Link unlocks cards. On the Eidolon's last HP, choose Stay Inside, Hard Disconnect, or Emergency Overclock.
Help.Competencies: Competencies: your class grants Full Access to one; cyberware can grant Card Access, Half Access (up to half your level), or Full Access.

Help.Members: Members: drag the characters into the Party's members tab.
Help.Reputation: Reputation: starts at +2 and rises +1 with each new Crew Tier. It shows up as an Experience on each member's sheet.
Help.Assets: Crew Assets: vehicles, safehouses, gear, and rewards live in the Party Inventory. They stay with the Crew when someone leaves.
Help.NewCharacter: New character: starts at the lowest level of the current Tier (Tier 1 → level 1, Tier 2 → 2, Tier 3 → 5, Tier 4 → 8).
Help.Buttons: Chat buttons: Get Them Out applies to the targeted ally; Back Me Up rolls the selected character's reaction; Hidden Cache puts 3 Supplies in the Inventory; Sabotage Package has the GM's restore button (2 Fear); a Tag Team Roll with Hope offers +1 Edge.
Help.AllIn: All In: opens the Tag Team Roll with no Hope cost; when it ends, whoever rolled clears 1 Stress.

Move.teamwork: The first time in each scene a character Helps an Ally, their advantage die is a d8 instead of a d6. When a character starts a Group Action Roll, the characters can split the Hope spent.
Move.backMeUp: When a Crew member fails an action roll, another member can step in: they move within Close range and make a relevant reaction roll, describing how they save the situation. On a success, the original roll becomes a success with Fear.
Move.getThemOut: When a Crew member within Close range would mark Hit Points or become Vulnerable or Restrained, another character moves within Very Close range of them. Reduce the HP marked by 1 or clear one temporary condition. Then move both within Close range toward cover, a vehicle, an exit, or a safer position.
Move.planB: Reveal a plausible contingency plan the Crew prepared for the Contract.
Move.allIn: Two Crew members make a Tag Team Roll without spending Hope, even if they already made one this session. Afterward, each character who took part clears 1 Stress.

Option.hiddenCache: Gain three Supply tokens. Spend one to produce a common consumable, weapon, or tool.
Option.insideAccess: Create a Breach against the local network or security system. The next roll made to exploit it gains +4.
Option.sabotagePackage: Disable a connected system until the GM spends 2 Fear to restore it.
Option.escapeVector: Establish an extraction route within Far range. The group can leave the scene without another roll.

Gains.tagTeam: A Tag Team Roll succeeds with Hope.
Gains.protect: A character marks HP, Stress, or accepts a serious consequence to protect another Crew member.
Gains.crewFirst: A character puts the Crew above their own safety or reward.
Gains.cooperation: The Crew completes an important part of the Contract through cooperation.
